correctness.rationale: Optimizing the quadratic opinion payoff conditional on a binary action yields exactly x_i^+=1 iff (Wy)_i>theta=(1+q)/2, y^+=cWy+(1-c)x^+. Prescribed opposite-community alternating actions force a unique two-phase opinion solution because the two-step affine matrix c^2W^2 is a contraction, and permutation/block swap symmetry forces two block values L,H with H-L=(1-c)/(1-c+2cp). The strict switching condition is equivalent to p<(1-c)(1-q)/(2(1-c+cq)); at equality the tie-to-defect rule excludes this pattern. In the strict chamber c^2W^2 contracts all opinion directions, giving local exponential attraction and parameter robustness; both consensus equilibria also contract locally. An independently recomputed rational n=4 witness has p=1/4,c=1/2,q=2/9, theta=11/18 and 1/6–5/6 swapped opinions with input means 2/3,1/3. No claim about all possible cycles is proven.

originality.rationale: Davidson et al. supply the public-goods best-response game and focus on equilibrium/convergence under restricted conditions. A genuine earlier October 12 Resultary theorem already constructs attracting two-cycles on a fully positive symmetric four-player complete network, including an equivalent four-player open-region condition, so mere possibility or n=4 robustness is NOT new. An October 18 theorem constructs arbitrary-period cycles on directed cyclic/nearly permutation networks. Neither gives the uniform all-even-population two-community necessary-and-sufficient patterned p cutoff or class uniqueness; those are the surviving originally motivated classification. This is qualified best-knowledge novelty, not a novelty claim for cycles in general.
residual_risks: Originality concerns the all-even-n sharp patterned-class threshold, not generic two-cycles, n=4 existence, or complete classification of all attractors.
Unindexed equivalent all-size block-reduction work may exist; priority is best-of-knowledge.
Tie defection at exact threshold is essential; p in [0,1), q in (0,1), m>=2 and simultaneous updates.

value.rationale: The all-size exact intercommunity mixing threshold isolates the structural condition for a stable cooperative alternation in a standard coupled continuous-opinion/public-goods model; it distinguishes coexistence of three attractors from consensus predictions and controls a genuine chamber boundary. Since the exact threshold/uniqueness hold for every even n on positive weighted connected networks, the classification is mathematically useful beyond the known four-agent example.
